contexts.name: access-control
contexts.description: Multi-layer access control enforcing scope, path safety, platform rules, and tier gating. The scope_enforcement module checks whether a persona's requested action falls within its declared capability scope; path_safety validates file paths against allowed directories; platform_rules applies OS-specific restrictions; tier controls feature availability per subscription level; desktop_security gates which native app bridges may be invoked.

contexts.name: account-cloud-sync
contexts.description: Handles user account lifecycle and cloud data synchronisation: Google OAuth sign-in/sign-out flows, telemetry opt-in/opt-out toggle, and manual app update checking with version history. When authenticated, renders a cloud sync dashboard showing per-table sync state, last sync timestamp, total rows synced across all tracked tables, and a Sync Now trigger. Calls the cloudSync API module which maps to a Supabase-backed Rust sync writer. Depends on the app's auth store for session state.

contexts.name: api-key-management
contexts.description: Manages API keys that third-party MCP clients use to authenticate against the local HTTP management server (port 9420). Handles full key lifecycle: creation with scoped permissions and optional expiry, one-time plaintext reveal dialog, soft revocation with audit trail, hard deletion, stale-key detection, and per-key audit log drawer. Also manages origin-bound 'Connected Apps' (cloud application OAuth-style pairings) and an MCP server liveness status panel. Depends on the external_api_keys and pairing command modules in Rust.
contexts.api_surface: createExternalApiKey, listExternalApiKeys, revokeExternalApiKey, deleteExternalApiKey, listApiKeyAudit; revokePairing; probeMcpServer (http://127.0.0.1:9420)

contexts.name: api-proxy-access
contexts.description: Credential-authenticated HTTP proxy and resource access layer: proxies arbitrary HTTP requests through a credential's auth strategy with per-credential token-bucket rate limiting and aggregate latency/error metrics; provides the unified Capability trait for DB queries (Supabase, Neon, Upstash, PlanetScale) and resource-picker listing (repos, projects, tables). All three surfaces share the same resolve-credential → execute → audit-log pattern.
contexts.api_surface: proxy_request (Tauri command), query_database (Tauri command), list_resources (Tauri command)

contexts.name: auth-session-api
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for user authentication (Google OAuth login/logout, session state), external API key lifecycle (create, list, audit — used by the management HTTP API on port 9420), device pairing approvals (web dashboard ↔ desktop handshakes), CLI credential capture (running service auth flows in a subprocess), and ambient auth detection (discovering which services the user is already authenticated with). These form the identity and access layer.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: login_with_google, get_auth_state, create_external_api_key, approve_pairing, cli_capture_run, detect_authenticated_services

contexts.name: connector-discovery-api
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for connector definition CRUD (the schema objects that describe how to authenticate with an external service — field definitions, credential types, healthcheck rules) and connector discovery (dynamically enumerating sub-resources within an authenticated connector, e.g. listing Sentry projects or GitHub repos to populate adoption questionnaire pickers). Connectors are the bridge between credentials and services.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_connectors, create_connector, update_connector, discover_connector_resources

contexts.name: connector-management
contexts.description: Connector definition lifecycle — creating, discovering, and managing connector schemas that declare how a credential maps to an external service. Includes credential-recipe design (AI-generates a connector schema from an OpenAPI spec or description) and schema proposals.

contexts.name: core-crypto-redact
contexts.description: Provides AES-256-GCM symmetric encryption and RSA session-key pair generation for securing credentials over the IPC bridge, a conservative secret-redaction pass that scrubs high-confidence credential patterns and high-entropy tokens from stored execution traces, and the ring-buffer healthcheck ledger primitives for tracking per-credential liveness over the last 20 checks.

contexts.name: credential-acquisition-api
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the multiple pathways to acquire and populate credentials: OAuth gateway flows (Google, generic providers), automated browser-based credential capture (Chromium subprocess, 11-min timeout), AI-guided credential design, and credential recipe caching (connector → field prefill recipes ranked by usage). Together these minimize friction in getting a credential from zero to healthcheck-passing.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: start_google_credential_oauth, start_auto_cred_browser, start_credential_design, get_credential_recipe, upsert_credential_recipe

contexts.name: credential-auth
contexts.description: Authentication and credential acquisition flows — OAuth browser flow, CLI token capture, automatic credential detection from running processes, desktop keychain bridge, foraging (scanning local configs for existing keys), and negotiator (interactive step-by-step credential setup). These commands bring credentials in from the environment.

contexts.name: credential-connector-models
contexts.description: Domain types for the entire credential and connector surface: `Credential`, `LedgerHealthEntry` (ring buffer row), `CredentialRecipe` (parameterised rotation recipe), `ConnectorDefinition` (capability contract), `ExternalApiKey`, `OAuthTokenMetric`, and `RotationPolicy`. These are the canonical structs shared between the security commands, the vault UI, and the rotation engine.

contexts.name: credential-core-api
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the core credential store: CRUD for persona credentials (AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest), bulk and per-credential healthchecks against live services, vault status and migration, and credential rotation policy management (scheduled key rotation, anomaly scoring, OAuth token lifecycle metrics). This is the authoritative read/write surface for the encrypted vault.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_credentials, create_credential, update_credential, healthcheck_credential, get_vault_status, list_rotation_policies

contexts.name: credential-intelligence
contexts.description: AI-assisted credential intelligence commands — natural-language vault queries, debug helpers, API proxy (relays requests through stored credentials), AI artifact flow for credential generation, external API key management, and OpenAPI autopilot (reads a spec and auto-configures credential requirements).

contexts.name: credential-lifecycle
contexts.description: Credential lifecycle management: windowed-anomaly healthchecks with sliding 5m/1h/24h failure-rate windows, OAuth token proactive refresh before expiry with per-refresh observability metrics, credential rotation policies, and the connector-strategy registry that consolidates healthcheck, rotation, and token-refresh logic into one extension point per connector type.

contexts.name: credential-negotiation
contexts.description: Design-time credential modeling and runtime negotiation between personas and their required connectors. The credential_design module defines the credential schema and UI hint types for the design surface; credential_negotiator resolves which credentials are available, missing, or need re-auth before execution starts, and surfaces structured gap reports to the frontend.

contexts.name: credential-negotiator
contexts.description: Auto-discovery and negotiation layer for credentials — scans the environment (browser profiles, OS credential stores, environment variables) to suggest matching credentials for a connector, reducing manual setup friction.

contexts.name: credential-scoping-api
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for credential resource scoping (pinning a credential to a subset of its available sub-resources, e.g. a GitHub PAT limited to two repos), MCP gateway membership management (bundling multiple MCP-speaking credentials under one gateway attachment point for persona tool routing), and cryptographic document signing (peer-to-peer document signature creation and verification). These are advanced credential access-control primitives.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_gateway_members, add_gateway_member, list_connector_resources, set_scoped_resources, sign_document, verify_document

contexts.name: credential-vault
contexts.description: Encrypted credential storage with AES-256-GCM. Manages secret creation, retrieval, OS keyring integration, and the vault catalog UI. All connector credentials flow through the vault; bindings are validated against connector requirements before execution.

contexts.name: credentials-repo
contexts.description: Repository for vault credentials — encrypted storage of API keys, OAuth tokens, and service authentication data. Manages AES-256-GCM encrypted credential blobs, IV storage, and credential metadata. Serves as the secure backing store for the Connector Catalog and Vault features.

contexts.name: identity-oauth-repo
contexts.description: Repositories for user identity management, OAuth token lifecycle tracking, and OAuth metrics. Stores identity provider bindings, token refresh history, and per-provider token usage metrics that feed into credential health monitoring.

contexts.name: mcp-gateway
contexts.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) gateway and tools bridge — exposes credentials and persona capabilities as MCP-compatible resources and tools, and manages the vector knowledge base used for semantic credential search. Allows external MCP clients to use Personas as a credential provider.

contexts.name: oauth-flow-hooks
contexts.description: Composable hooks for driving OAuth consent flows: a low-level polling hook with AbortController lifecycle and ref-based secret storage, a protocol-level wrapper that adds onComplete/onError callbacks, a consent-step hook, and a universal OAuth composable for any provider. Credentials are kept in refs rather than state to prevent DevTools and Sentry exposure.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri OAuth commands; external OAuth provider redirect URLs

contexts.name: oauth-gateway
contexts.description: OAuth 2.0 PKCE flow implementation for connecting third-party services. Manages authorization initiation, callback handling, token refresh with distributed locking, and the browser-side credential capture bridge.

contexts.name: oauth-token-management
contexts.description: Google OAuth 2.0 flow and token refresh management for connector authentication. google_oauth handles the full authorization code flow, token exchange, and refresh; oauth_refresh_lock serializes concurrent refresh attempts to prevent token churn; pairing handles device pairing codes for cross-device authentication bootstrap.

contexts.name: p2p-identity-enclave
contexts.description: P2P identity and encrypted enclave for the Invisible Apps peer network. The identity module manages device keypairs, peer certificates, and trust anchors; the enclave module implements the encrypted data partition for persona secrets that travel over the QUIC transport. Both are compiled only when the p2p feature is enabled.

contexts.name: prompt-injection-defense
contexts.description: Shared primitives for preventing prompt injection when user-controlled text is embedded into AI prompts. Strips structural patterns (section delimiters, role overrides, jailbreak phrases) and escapes special characters. Used as the single source of truth by both variableSanitizer and workflowSanitizer so their protections stay in sync.

contexts.name: security-audit-repo
contexts.description: Repositories for security audit logging — tracks credential access, API key usage patterns, settings changes, and rotation schedules. Provides the audit trail operators need for compliance review and detecting unauthorized access patterns.

contexts.name: sensitive-data-masking
contexts.description: Masks sensitive values in JSON payloads and error messages before they are rendered in the UI or sent to Sentry. Redacts keys matching patterns like password, token, api_key, and connection_string, and strips file paths, IP addresses, and internal hostnames from error text. Used by crash persistence, error display, and cloud review flows.

contexts.name: url-html-sanitization
contexts.description: Sanitizes URLs (blocking private network ranges, unsafe protocols, embedded credentials, and unicode bidi overrides) and HTML (using DOMPurify, allowing only highlight.js span tags) before rendering in the UI. Prevents SSRF, tracking pixels, and XSS from AI-generated or external content.

contexts.name: vault-api-playground-shell
contexts.description: Interactive API playground modal shell for testing connector credentials against live endpoints. CredentialPlaygroundModal is the root; PlaygroundHeader shows connector identity; RequestBuilder and BuilderParams construct HTTP requests; ResponseViewer renders the raw response; EndpointRow lists available endpoints; useApiTestRunner drives the request execution and response state.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri IPC: run_api_test; calls external connector APIs via credential

contexts.name: vault-api-playground-tabs
contexts.description: Tab views within the API playground modal: Overview (connector summary, health), API Explorer (endpoint list, request firing, response viewer), MCP Tools (list/invoke MCP tools per server), Executions (recent test runs), and recipe creation flow. useApiExplorerState manages the explorer tab's selected endpoint and response history.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-autocred-session
contexts.description: Session management and adapter layer for the automated credential (AutoCred) Playwright-driven flow. useAutoCredSession maintains the phase FSM, extracted values, browser log entries, and adapter results. TauriPlaywrightAdapter wraps Playwright MCP calls into a swappable interface; helper functions handle error parsing and field completeness checks.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-autocred-ui
contexts.description: Automated credential harvesting UI that drives a Playwright browser session to extract API keys from a service's developer portal. The wizard walks through Consent→Browser→Review steps; AutoCredPanel is the root; BrowserDetail shows the live Playwright session; AutoCredReview lets the user confirm extracted values before saving.
contexts.api_surface: Playwright MCP: playwright_navigate, playwright_snapshot, playwright_fill, playwright_click

contexts.name: vault-catalog-design-modal
contexts.description: AI-driven credential design modal that analyzes a URL or service description and proposes a connector configuration. The modal walks through Idle→Analyzing→Preview→Done phases (each a separate component), shows recipe confidence banners, and renders setup instructions. CredentialDesignContext provides the orchestrator value to all phase components via context.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-design-orchestrator
contexts.description: Orchestrator logic and setup instruction rendering for the AI credential design flow. useCredentialDesignOrchestrator composes useCredentialDesign, useOAuthConsent, useUniversalOAuth, and useCredentialHealth into a single context value. Setup instruction helpers render markdown-formatted step-by-step guides fetched from the backend design result.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-desktop
contexts.description: Desktop app and local MCP server discovery panel. DesktopDiscoveryPanel scans the user's machine for installed apps (DesktopAppCard, DiscoveryAppList) and running MCP servers (McpServerCard, DiscoveryMcpList). CapabilityApprovalCard surfaces per-capability permission grants required before connecting a locally discovered service.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-foraging
contexts.description: Credential foraging feature that scans the user's environment (shell config, dotfiles, cloud CLIs) for existing credentials that can be auto-imported. ForagingPanel orchestrates the scan; ForagingConsent gates the operation behind user approval; ForagingResults and ForagingResultCard present discovered secrets; ForagingStepIndicator shows scan progress.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-forms
contexts.description: Catalog-level credential template forms for creating connector credentials from a pre-defined template. CredentialTemplateForm is the main form; CredentialTypePicker selects the connector type; CodebaseProjectPicker and ProjectList handle project-scoped connectors; TemplateFormBody renders the field layout.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-negotiator
contexts.description: AI-guided connector setup negotiator that interactively walks a user through multi-step configuration. NegotiatorPanel is the root; NegotiatorPhases renders Guiding or Planning phases; NegotiatorStepCard shows each step with its status; StepActions provides approve/skip/retry controls. negotiatorMotion defines the animation presets for step transitions.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-picker
contexts.description: The main connector catalog grid that lets users browse, search, and filter available connector types before adding a credential. CredentialPicker is the root; PickerGrid renders connector cards; CredentialPickerFilters provides role-based and category filtering; usePickerFilters drives filter state; useRecipeIndicators shows which connectors already have recipes.

contexts.name: vault-catalog-schemas
contexts.description: Connector schema-driven form rendering. CredentialSchemaForm renders a dynamic form from a connector's JSON auth schema; SchemaFormFields maps schema field types to React inputs; ExtraFieldRenderers handles non-standard field types; McpPrefilledForm pre-fills known MCP server fields; schemaConfigs centralizes per-connector field overrides.

contexts.name: vault-credential-card-banners
contexts.description: Credential card-level status indicators and action banners. CompositeHealthDot renders a multi-signal health dot; ReauthBanner prompts re-authentication when a token is revoked; ScopeMismatchBanner warns when a saved credential lacks required scopes; VaultErrorBanner surfaces vault-level errors; CredentialDeleteDialog handles soft-delete with undo.

contexts.name: vault-credential-health-intel
contexts.description: Credential intelligence panels displayed in the credential detail view. Covers anomaly score display, audit log table, scope section, event template configuration, and the CredentialIntelligence aggregate panel. These surfaces give operators visibility into credential usage patterns and abnormal activity detected by the backend.

contexts.name: vault-credential-import
contexts.description: Multi-step credential import wizard that lets users bulk-import secrets from files, cloud secret managers, or other external sources. ImportSourcePicker selects the source type; ImportInputPhase handles raw input; ImportPreview shows a diff before committing; ImportSyncConfig configures ongoing sync; useCredentialImport drives the wizard state machine.

contexts.name: vault-credential-resource-picker
contexts.description: Reusable resource picker component that appears after saving a credential, allowing users to immediately link the new credential to a cloud resource (e.g. a specific S3 bucket or GitHub repo). resourcePickerStore is a lightweight Zustand slice holding picker visibility and target state; usePostSaveResourcePicker bridges the save flow to picker open.

contexts.name: vault-credential-rotation
contexts.description: Credential secret rotation UI. CredentialRotationSection is the main detail panel showing rotation history and anomaly score; RotationPolicyControls, RotationNewPolicy, and RotationActivePolicy manage creating and viewing rotation schedules; RotationCountdownRing renders a visual countdown timer to the next scheduled rotation.

contexts.name: vault-credential-team-access
contexts.description: Team and workspace credential sharing surfaces. GatewayMembersModal manages which team members have access to a shared gateway credential; PendingAuthModal handles pending authorization requests from collaborators. WorkspaceConnectPanel and ProviderSection enable connecting workspace providers (GitHub, Slack, Google Workspace) so their credentials are shared across a team.

contexts.name: vault-credentials-form
contexts.description: Credential creation and editing forms, covering auth-method tabs (API key, OAuth, basic, MCP), field capture rows, connection-test section, OAuth progress ring, and setup guide. ConnectorCredentialModal is the primary modal; CredentialEditForm handles the form state. Renders different field renderers depending on the connector's authentication schema.

contexts.name: vault-credentials-list
contexts.description: Credential list view with column definitions, filtering, detail modal wiring, and empty state. CredentialList renders the sortable/filterable table of stored credentials; CredentialListColumns defines the column schema (name, connector, health status, last-used); useCredentialListFilters provides client-side search and filter logic.

contexts.name: vault-credentials-manager
contexts.description: Top-level credential manager shell that coordinates the full credential management workflow. Orchestrates the credential list, add-views, breadcrumb navigation, trust badge, rotate-all action, undo-delete, and re-auth banner. useCredentialManagerState drives the FSM (list / add / detail views) via a reducer dispatch; CredentialManagerViews renders the active view.

contexts.name: vault-credentials-state
contexts.description: Slice managing encrypted credential storage — listing, creating, updating, deleting, and healthchecking credential records and their associated connectors. Implements a 30-second cached fetch to deduplicate concurrent IPC calls from multiple components, with optimistic mutations and tombstone-based delete protection.

contexts.name: vault-database-state
contexts.description: Slice for database connector management — tracking configured database connections (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, etc.) that agent personas can query. Manages connection testing, schema discovery, and table listing for the Database Explorer feature.

contexts.name: vault-dependency-graph
contexts.description: Interactive credential relationship graph showing how credentials are connected to personas, recipes, and other credentials. CredentialRelationshipGraph is the root; GraphCanvas renders a force-directed D3 layout; BlastRadiusPanel shows impact analysis when a credential is revoked; SimulationPanel and SimulationControls let the user model revocation scenarios; credentialGraph.ts contains the pure graph algorithms.

contexts.name: vault-intelligence-api
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for AI-powered vault intelligence features: credential foraging (scanning system sources like browser keychains and env files to discover importable credentials), AI credential negotiation (guided step-by-step field collection for complex connectors), and the vector knowledge base (CRUD, semantic search, document ingestion, entity extraction, and embedding-backed retrieval). These features layer intelligent assistance over the raw credential and knowledge stores.
contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: scan_credential_sources, import_foraged_credential, start_credential_negotiation, create_knowledge_base, kb_search, kb_ingest_file

contexts.name: vault-root-components
contexts.description: Top-level vault UI entry points shared across the credential and catalog sub-features. Provides the VaultConnectorPicker for selecting connectors, CredentialPickerCards for card-style credential selection, and SetupStatusBadge to surface connector setup progress. Consumed by agent editors and other features that need to attach a credential.

contexts.name: vault-rotation-state
contexts.description: Slices managing credential rotation policies, automation workflows tied to credentials, and catalog UI preferences (filters, sort order, view mode). The rotation slice tracks scheduled and on-demand rotation jobs; the rotationOverview selector derives summary stats for the catalog header.

contexts.name: vault-shared-hooks
contexts.description: Cross-cutting React hooks shared by all vault sub-features. Covers credential OAuth flows (Google, universal), credential renaming, tag management, undo-delete, rotation ticker, vault status polling with module-level IPC cache, credential view FSM, navigation context, and the three-state health-check system (bulk healthcheck, per-credential health, and remediation evaluator). Acts as the primary shared hook library for vault UI state.
contexts.api_surface: Wraps IPC: vaultStatus, credential health, bulk healthcheck, OAuth consent

contexts.name: vault-shared-utils
contexts.description: Pure utility functions used throughout the vault feature. Provides auth-method style maps (icon, color, label per auth type), a three-state credential health score calculator, and tag normalization helpers. Also contains the unit test suite for the health score logic.

contexts.name: vault-store-root
contexts.description: Top-level Zustand store composing the vault domain — credentials, database connectors, automations, rotation policies, and catalog UI preferences. Provides the unified store interface for all secrets management and connector features.

contexts.name: vault-vector-kb-ingest
contexts.description: Document ingestion and entity extraction UI for the vector knowledge base. IngestDropZone and IngestDirectoryPicker handle file/folder input; IngestProgressBar shows chunking/embedding progress; IngestTextModal accepts pasted text; EntityTable and SchemaEditor support structured extraction of entities from ingested documents into typed tables.

contexts.name: vault-vector-kb-shell
contexts.description: Vector knowledge base modal shell and tab surfaces for credentials that back a knowledge base (e.g. a file store). VectorKbModal is the root 4-tab modal (Documents, Search, Extract, Settings); tabs handle document listing, semantic search, entity extraction, settings configuration, and corpus overview; StatusBadge shows KB indexing state.
